prompt: The pilot's log (5 games, 1W 4L, all debriefed) reads: mana was the loss twice (Blood Moon, closed by the pilot's decision; no green source, a mulligan rule), and the TELEGRAPH was the loss three times -- 'I ramped fast enough to broadcast the win before I could present lethal', 'the treasure pile plus fireballing every ETB made me the obvious problem', 'I pour it into the board too early and telegraph'. His verdict: 'speed without protection or politics makes me the obvious kill target before I can close', and after the refactor 'I now have zero responses' (no counterspells; protection is Swat, Teferi's, Heroic Intervention, Boros Charm, Greaves). His four research asks, verbatim: (a) dragons that grant haste to the board -- 'the problem is speed, not size'; (b) haste enablers generally -- 'Terror has to swing the turn it lands, not sit'; (c) protection density -- 'some lock-down (equipment indestructible?) that does not cost me dragon slots'; (d) dragons with ETB counters or flash, and protection on dragons or dragon enchantments, without slowing the deck down. Measured: Forge at standard-v3 0.353 [0.215, 0.521] over 40 games, engine played, piloting comparable, killed by combat damage at mean global turn 35, the commander resolved in 57% of games at global turn 27; the goldfish reads kill_by_8 0.79 and the commander cast by t6 only 33% (mean t6.9), 4 of 22 Dragons have haste; the audit reads card-advantage 4 (target 10), colour-sources -12 on the worst colour, interaction-breadth 4 of 5, ramp 22 (over), protection 8 (over by count but not by the pilot's read). What changes make this deck close faster than the table can converge on it -- haste so the dragons swing the turn they land, protection that does not cost dragon slots, responses -- and which of those does the evidence support, with every add named against the axis it closes and every cut priced? Ownership is not a constraint. No two-card infinites.
reading: The pilot asks what lets this deck close before the table converges — haste so a Dragon swings the turn it lands, protection that costs no Dragon slot, and responses — and the evidence says the deck is already fast enough to be seen: ramp reads 22 against a 10–12 target, the goldfish kills by turn 8 in 0.792 of games, and the log names the telegraph as the loss in 003, 004 and 005 in the pilot's own words ('I ramped fast enough to broadcast the win before I could actually present lethal'). The 'four hasty Dragons' premise undercounts — Dragon Tempest and Temur Ascendancy already grant haste board-wide — but a two-card group is in 0.137 of opening sevens by the audit's own hypergeometric, so the haste ask is a redundancy problem, not an absence; and the pilot's 'zero responses' is exact where the audit's 'protection 8, over' is not, because all eight are protection effects and none of the nine interaction copies is a counterspell. Forge at standard-v3 agrees on the mechanism: 0.353 [0.215, 0.521] over 40 games, all 19 eliminations by damage at mean global turn 35.0 (ci95 [32.53, 37.47]), the commander first resolving at mean global turn 27.17 in the 0.575 of games it resolved at all, interaction cast 0.17 a game against 0.35 received — the deck presents, is converged on, and loses a damage race it started. So the ranking below trades ramp and slow top-end for flash, haste and counters — 'fast to build' into 'fast to close' — and the piloting half (hold the tempo, sequence the tell last, point the table at the quiet assembler) is routed to the handbook as an open question, not to a card.

open_questions.question: A table-politics layer for the handbook (the pilot's ask (d) in 003): how a deck that visibly presents the biggest board manages its perceived threat — hold the tempo a turn ('drop the tempo a turn or two and hold Twin Flame until the dragons are actually there', 005), sequence the tell last, keep instant-speed mana open, and point the table at the quiet assembler (004). This is a procedures page for poh-procedures, not a card; the strategy corpus already holds the frame (multiplayer.threat-deflection, multiplayer.pivot-window, multiplayer.pod-management) and needs applying to this deck's tells: Terror of the Peaks, the Treasure pile, Gadrak, the commander.
open_questions.why_it_matters: Three of five logged losses are filed as 'politics' or telegraph by the pilot himself; no card in this list changes that, and a prescription that only buys cards for a piloting loss would be misrouting the finding.

open_questions.question: Declare a 'Board-wide haste source drawn' any_of group in goldfish_targets.json (Dragon Tempest, Temur Ascendancy, plus any haste add a branch takes) so the assembly rate is measured rather than priced here by hypergeometric; and model the board-wide haste grant in goldfish.combat_profile, which today reads haste only from a creature's own text, so that kill_by_8 can move when a grant is added.
open_questions.why_it_matters: Eight of the ten adds are invisible to the goldfish as written; a branch aimed at kill_by_8 with a haste objective will read 'not met' whatever it does until the model applies the grant. Until then Forge is the only measure, and its 40-game interval [0.215, 0.521] cannot resolve a swap.

open_questions.question: Transcendent Dragon cast with flash under Miirym and Panharmonicon in response to a wipe: does the Miirym token copy also counter a spell? Its ETB reads 'if you cast it', and the copy is not cast — and Panharmonicon doubles the original's trigger. A stack scenario is needed before any handbook line claims two counters.
open_questions.why_it_matters: The card is bought as a response; how many responses one cast is worth decides whether it is a Negate on a body or the deck's best defensive turn.

open_questions.question: Rhythm of the Wild's riot on Miirym copies and Lathliss tokens: riot reads 'Nontoken creatures you control', so a token copy takes neither the counter nor haste from Rhythm — but Dragon Tempest grants the copy haste if it flies. Does a copied Terror of the Peaks under Rhythm + Tempest attack the turn it enters, and what does the riot choice (counter or haste) do to a Dragon that already has haste from Tempest?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The first-ranked add's value on the deck's copy engine is unproven, and the handbook should say which riot mode to choose on a hasty flyer.

open_questions.question: How often does a keepable seven for this list contain no green source? The pilot's proposed mulligan rule in 005 — 'no green source, consider shipping it' — needs a rate before it becomes a rule; the goldfish keeps 0.792 of first sevens but its mulligan is colour-blind.
open_questions.why_it_matters: Two of five logged losses are mana (001 Blood Moon, closed; 005 no green). The rule is the pilot's, and a rate is what turns it from a hunch into a handbook line.

gaps: No deck_recon.json exists for ur-dragon (audit freshness: recon.present false), so no per-commander inclusion rates were consulted; every add here is mined from the corpus by oracle text and identity. A recon pass would rank these against what Ur-Dragon lists actually run.

Forge never cast Teferi's Protection or Deflecting Swat in 40 games (both absent from engine_casts.by_card), so the harness has no measurement of the protection class on this list and a Forge run cannot validate a protection add; the goldfish cannot see protection at all.

The goldfish reads two things in this list — Kolaghan's own haste and the Dragon bodies. Riot, flash, board-wide haste grants, counters and protection are all outside the model. Forge is the gate for eight of the ten, and the standard-v3 record is 40 games with an interval of 0.306 width; the swap effect it would need to see is smaller than that.

Both goldfish kill targets are labelled UNVERIFIED and no checker-passed stack proves a kill on this list; three passing stacks (003, 004, 006) describe boards the deck can no longer make. 'Close faster' is being prescribed for a kill nobody has proven.
Black colour-sources are 12 short of target; two adds (Dragonlord Kolaghan, Call the Spirit Dragons) add a black pip. mana-fit on the branch is the check, and the goldfish cannot rank lands.

The validator recomputes ramp, protection and interaction by role for the paired swaps; colour-sources, mana-sources and the haste group are not recomputed, so the Skyshroud Claim and Faeburrow Elder costs are stated, not measured.

Rhythm of the Wild's riot half is supported (oracle: 'Nontoken creatures you control have riot'; Dragon Tempest and Temur Ascendancy confirmed as the two existing board-wide grants). The uncounterable half is sold as 'the counter-proofing half of ask (d)' — 005's ask (d) is 'dragons with ETB counters or flash, and protection on dragons or dragon enchantments', i.e. the pilot HOLDING counters; no log entry (001–005) records an opponent countering anything the pilot cast. The why's 'a table that ran three counterspells' worth of answers out of this deck in the refactor' is not in the log — 005 says the refactor removed the pilot's OWN counterspells. The card is a fine haste add; the second job answers nothing in the evidence.

'with any Dragon on the battlefield (all 22 have power 4 or more) Ferocious makes it a one-mana hard counter' — cards.json: Firespitter Whelp 2/2, Thrakkus the Butcher 3/4, Ganax, Astral Hunter 3/4, Twinflame Tyrant 3/5. 18 of the 22 Dragons (counting the commander) have power ≥ 4; with only a Whelp or Gadrak-less early board Stubborn Denial is a one-mana tax, not a hard counter. The 0-of-9-counterspell claim is supported: no card in the 99 carries 'counter target' text.

cost_of_cutting: 'Terror of the Peaks and Scourge of Valkas triggers each lose a point of damage per Dragon entering' — cards.json oracle for Scourge of Valkas: 'deals X damage to any target, where X is the number of Dragons you control'. It is count-based; losing the +1/+1 anthem costs Valkas nothing. Only Terror (damage equal to the entering creature's power) loses a point. Forge cast 11 of 40 matches engine_casts.by_card.
